headline: A Workspace Auditor for OpenClaw AI Agent Configurations
lede: A developer who spent six weeks running AI agents through OpenClaw has released a free command-line tool — called Souls CLI — that audits and grades agent workspace configurations. The tool assigns letter grades to each workspace and promises measurable improvements in how an agent reasons and responds, in roughly five minutes. It targets both solo and multi-agent deployments.
body:
**OpenClaw** is an AI gateway platform that connects autonomous agents to messaging channels — WhatsApp, Slack, Discord, and more than twenty others. Each agent runs inside its own isolated *workspace*: a directory of configuration files, including `SOUL.md`, a personality guide that shapes how the agent thinks, what it knows about itself, and how it behaves across conversations. The quality of that file, and the surrounding workspace, largely determines how coherent and useful the agent is in practice.

The problem @tolibear_ is addressing is mundane but real. Most users copy a starter config, tweak a few lines, and move on. After six weeks of intensive use, the developer noticed that poorly structured `SOUL.md` files and incomplete workspace setups produce agents that drift, forget context, or respond inconsistently. Souls CLI is the diagnostic layer missing from OpenClaw's default tooling.

The interface — visible in the screenshot — is a terminal UI that lists every workspace the user has created, each next to a percentage score and a letter grade. Grades in the demo range from 85 (B) down to 45 (F), giving users an immediate triage view. From there, the tool can audit a single workspace or all of them in sequence, surfacing specific weaknesses rather than just a score.

In OpenClaw's multi-agent model, each agent has its own state directory, session history, and auth profiles stored under `~/.openclaw/agents/<agentId>/`. A misconfigured workspace in a multi-agent setup can corrupt routing — messages reaching the wrong agent, or an agent responding without the right persona context. Souls CLI appears to inspect these per-agent configurations, not just the top-level `SOUL.md`, making it relevant to more complex deployments.

The claim that improvements take "five minutes" is worth mild skepticism: the audit is automated, but acting on its recommendations still requires editing configuration files by hand. The grading criteria and the specific AI research behind the scoring are not disclosed in the tweet, so users are taking the methodology on trust. The tool is free and launching at `souls.zip`, which lowers the barrier to trying it.

concepts.definition: A plain-text configuration file used by OpenClaw to define an AI agent's personality, identity, and behavioral rules. It acts as a persistent system prompt that shapes how the agent responds across all conversations. OpenClaw's documentation describes it as the agent's 'personality guide.'

In OpenClaw, each agent has a dedicated on-disk directory (under `~/.openclaw/agents/<agentId>/`) containing its configuration files, session history, auth profiles, and local notes. The workspace is the full context that determines an agent's identity and memory — separate workspaces mean separate, isolated agents.

A feature of OpenClaw that allows multiple distinct agents — each with its own workspace and persona — to run inside a single gateway. Inbound messages from different channels or users are routed to the appropriate agent via bindings. This enables, for example, one WhatsApp number to be handled by different agents depending on who is messaging.

A text-based graphical interface that runs inside a terminal emulator, using keyboard navigation instead of a mouse. TUIs offer the interactivity of a GUI without requiring a web browser or desktop environment, making them popular for developer tools.
